title: How To Build Effortless Rapport With Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that genuine, behavior-influencing rapport is less about proactive bonding activities and more about what a teacher refrains from doing—namely causing friction through yelling, scolding, or sarcasm. Rapport, he explains, develops naturally and organically from day one when a teacher is simply pleasant, and it is most fragile and consequential during the early behavioral tests students inevitably run. He describes how rapport can collapse quickly once students witness inconsistency, lectures, or broken promises, turning a warm relationship into a wary, guarded one. His prescription combines a genuine enjoyment of students with an unwavering, near-obsessive commitment to the classroom management plan, which together create durable rapport without requiring charisma or extra effort.
points: Rapport is built less by proactive bonding activities and more by avoiding friction—refraining from yelling, scolding, and sarcasm.
Rapport develops organically from the first day of school and strengthens (or breaks) fastest during students' early behavioral testing.
Rapport can be lost quickly once students witness inconsistency, lectures, unenforced rules, or broken promises.
Building lasting rapport doesn't require comedic talent or extra effort—it requires enjoying students combined with strict reliance on the classroom management plan.
Rapport gives a classroom management plan its 'teeth,' making students genuinely reluctant to disappoint the teacher.
quotes: Rapport provides the good vibrations between you and your class that makes your classroom management plan matter.
The simple truth is that the better rapport you have with your students, the easier classroom management becomes.
You see, rapport comes effortlessly to those who manage their classroom without causing friction with students.
Like clockwork, students will begin testing the behavioral waters early in the school year to see if you really do mean what you say.
And hereafter, with the once-bright rays of rapport all but faded, both parties begin the slow, guarded limp onward, day after day, wary of each other but just getting through it.
No, rapport is nothing more than a willingness to enjoy your students combined with a near-obsessive reliance on your classroom management plan.
